skill.name: scholar-evaluation
skill.description: Apply the ScholarEval framework to review academic papers, proposals, literature reviews, and scholarly drafts across structured research quality dimensions.
skill.summary: Evaluate scholarly work with structured criteria, scoring, and actionable revision feedback.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by academic rubric prose, markdown fences, inline file names, and a citation link. The real risks are optional Python command execution, a report writer that accepts user-controlled output paths, and a default recommendation to use an external diagram workflow. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve output paths under a dedicated reports directory, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and confirm before overwriting files.

remediation.issue: Executable Python commands in skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Mark script execution as optional and require explicit user confirmation before running Python commands from this skill.
Remove default diagram generation or gate it behind a clear user request. Document any external service or plugin dependency.

content.value_statement: Research feedback can be inconsistent across reviewers and criteria. This skill applies a structured ScholarEval workflow to review papers, proposals, and scholarly drafts.
actual_capabilities: Applies eight evaluation dimensions for questions, literature, methods, data, analysis, results, writing, and citations.
Provides strengths, weaknesses, critical issues, and prioritized recommendations.
Uses a 1 to 5 scoring rubric for dimension-level ratings.
Can calculate aggregate scores with the included Python score calculator.
Adapts evaluation scope to papers, proposals, reviews, theses, and abstracts.
References detailed rubric material in references/evaluation_framework.md.
limitations: It does not replace qualified peer review or discipline-specific expert judgment.
The score calculator can write reports to user-supplied paths and should be run carefully.
The referenced schematic generation command is not included in this skill package.
Citation quality checks depend on documents and sources provided by the user.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Manuscript Draft
use_cases.description: Review a research paper across core quality dimensions and receive prioritized revision guidance.

use_cases.title: Assess Publication Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether a paper meets expectations for a target journal, conference, or review venue.

use_cases.title: Review Proposal Quality
use_cases.description: Assess research questions, methods, feasibility, and expected contribution before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Paper Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a full draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this research paper with ScholarEval. Focus on overall quality, major strengths, and the top revision priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Methodology Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the methodology section only. Assess rigor, reproducibility, ethics, data quality, and alignment with the research questions.

prompt_templates.title: Score and Improve Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Score each applicable ScholarEval dimension from 1 to 5. Explain each score and list concrete changes that would raise it.

prompt_templates.title: Publication Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for a target venue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this manuscript for the target venue. Compare it against expected standards and give a ranked submission readiness plan.

output_examples.input: A user provides a research paper draft and asks for a comprehensive review.
output: Dimension scores with short evidence-based reasons.
Major strengths and critical weaknesses across the paper.
A prioritized revision plan for the next draft.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether a proposal is ready for conference submission.
output: A readiness assessment for the stated venue.
Risks in feasibility, novelty, methods, and expected contribution.
Specific fixes to address before submission.

output_examples.input: A user wants feedback on only the literature review section.
output: Coverage and synthesis feedback for the reviewed sources.
Missing perspectives or weak source choices.
Actionable suggestions to improve scholarly context.

best_practices: Provide the work type, target venue, and desired review scope before evaluation.
Ask for evidence-based feedback with section or page references.
Review any generated score report before using it in formal decisions.
anti_patterns: Treating the numeric score as a final publication decision.
Running the score calculator without checking the output file path.
Using the schematic command as a required step for every evaluation.

faq.question: What types of work can this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It can evaluate papers, proposals, literature reviews, theses, dissertations, conference abstracts, and short scholarly drafts.

faq.question: Does this replace peer review?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured feedback that should complement expert review and domain-specific judgment.

faq.question: Can it produce quantitative scores?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports 1 to 5 scores for applicable dimensions and can calculate aggregate scores with the included script.

faq.question: Does it verify citations automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can assess citation quality from provided materials, but it does not independently verify every source.

faq.question: Does it require running scripts?
faq.answer: No. Script use is optional for aggregate scoring, and users should approve any command before it runs.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
